Q: How should remote-agent tasks reconcile streaming status, reconnects and cancellation races?
A: An A2A task has an identity and lifecycle under the negotiated profile. Streamed updates help responsiveness but may be interrupted, so authoritative task readback and allowed transitions matter. Cancellation is a request whose effect depends on task state and remote support; it need not undo a completed external operation. Authenticate task access and scope continuation to the intended principal. Persist mapping between local and remote task identities, and distinguish unknown connectivity from a confirmed terminal result.
Why: A client disconnects after receiving 'working'. The remote task completes before cancellation arrives. On reconnect, read its actual terminal status instead of displaying 'cancelled' merely because a local cancel button was clicked.
Risk: A lost stream can cause duplicate task creation if identity mapping is discarded.
Trade: Durable remote task identity supports recovery at additional coordination cost.
Try: Interrupt the stream, request cancellation and reconcile the task through authoritative readback.
